What we'll cover

Sessions follow your exam board's specification and your target grade. These are the main areas.

Paper 1: Epistemology

  • What knowledge is
  • Perception
  • Reason as a source of knowledge
  • The limits of knowledge and scepticism

Paper 1: Moral philosophy

  • Utilitarianism
  • Kantian ethics
  • Aristotelian virtue ethics
  • Applied ethics
  • Meta-ethics

Paper 2: Metaphysics of God

  • Arguments for the existence of God
  • The attributes of God
  • The problem of evil
  • Religious language

Paper 2: Metaphysics of mind

  • Dualism
  • Physicalism
  • Functionalism
  • The problem of other minds
The exams

How the exams work

AQA A-level Philosophy is examined in two papers, each 3 hours and worth 100 marks. Paper 1 covers Epistemology and Moral philosophy; Paper 2 covers the Metaphysics of God and the Metaphysics of mind.

With that much writing time, the skill that separates grades is building a clear, sustained argument and weighing it, not listing everything you know.

Exam technique

Where marks are usually lost

  • Listing arguments instead of evaluating them
  • Skipping the strongest objections and the replies to them
  • Lopsided answers: all knowledge, very little judgement
  • Running short of time across a three-hour paper

FAQ

A-level Philosophy: common questions

Which specification do you teach?

AQA A-level Philosophy, the one I sat, scoring 196/200 across the two papers.

What does a top-mark essay look like?

A clear line of argument, precise use of the arguments and key terms, genuine engagement with objections, and a reasoned judgement at the end.

Do I need to have studied Philosophy before?

No. If you're at A-level, we start from what you've covered in school and build from there.
